source_text: Ecce ergo, in quantis humanae naturae necessariam Christi medicinam fatemur. At scio te vociferaturum cavillo tecum agi, non enim hanc te medicinam, qua corporibus subvenitur, sed nomine medicinae significasse Christi gratiam, quam a nobis affirmabas negari. Ad quod responderi potest tibi hoc ascribendum esse, qui rem, quam volebas intellegi, propriis noluisses signare nominibus. Sed quia vel tarde intellectum est, quam diceres medicinam, quam confuse nos negare mentitus eras, respondeamus et ad hoc, quod secundo intulisti, sicut et primo opere protestati sumus nos gratiam Christi, id est baptisma, ex quo ritum eius Christus instituit, ita necessariam omnibus in commune aetatibus confiteri, ut, quicumque eam utilem etiam parvulis negat, aeterno feriamus anathemate.
pass_a_gloss: Behold therefore in how many things we confess the medicine of Christ necessary to human nature. But I know you will cry out that it is dealt with you by a cavil, for you have not meant this medicine by which bodies are helped, but by the name of medicine you have signified the grace of Christ, which you were affirming is denied by us. To which it can be answered that this is to be ascribed to you, who would not have wanted to sign the thing which you wanted understood by proper names. But because even late it has been understood which medicine you were saying, which confusedly you had lied we deny, let us answer also to this which you brought in second, as also in the first work we have protested that we confess the grace of Christ, that is baptism, from which Christ instituted its rite, so necessary to all ages in common, that whoever denies it useful even to little ones we strike with eternal anathema.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'
LS parvulus; Blaise infants without usus rationis

pass_b_english: See, then, in how many respects we acknowledge Christ’s medicine necessary to human nature. But I know you will cry out that I am quibbling with you: you did not mean medicine that helps bodies; by ‘medicine’ you meant Christ’s grace, which you claimed we deny. You could be answered that this is your fault, since you refused to identify with proper terms what you wanted understood. Yet now that we have understood, even belatedly, which medicine you meant—the medicine you falsely and vaguely alleged we deny—let us answer this second point too. As we declared in our first work, we acknowledge Christ’s grace, that is, baptism, from the time Christ established its rite, to be necessary for all ages alike. We pronounce an eternal anathema on anyone who denies that it benefits even infants.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Keep the rite-name; Julian says praise of baptism is being used to smuggle natural evil.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
